answer:
Yes, there are several things to raise. The most urgent is your stool test. Your FIT (faecal immunochemical test) from 4 November 2025 was positive. A positive result normally means you need a colonoscopy to look at the bowel, and I cannot see a colonoscopy or any other follow-up test in your records since then. Please ask your doctor about this first, even if it was arranged and simply isn't recorded here.

Your diabetes checks look overdue. Your last HbA1c (a three-month blood sugar average) was 6.9% on 16 February 2026. It is usually checked every three to six months, and none has been recorded since. Your HbA1c also rose to 8.3% in January 2025. Your records show metformin ending in April 2024 and Jardiance starting in February 2025, with no diabetes medicine in between. Ask whether that gap was intended or is a gap in the records.

Your cholesterol has not been rechecked. LDL was 131 mg/dL in February 2025, the day before atorvastatin was started on 20 February 2025. There is no cholesterol test since then, so a follow-up is due. Ask whether 20 mg is the right dose for you, given your diabetes.

Some diabetes checks are not in your records at all: a urine albumin test and an eye exam. Your records also contain no vaccinations. Ask your doctor whether these were done somewhere else or are due now.
short: Positive FIT on 4 Nov 2025 with no colonoscopy recorded; HbA1c last checked 16 Feb 2026 (6.9%); LDL not rechecked since starting atorvastatin in Feb 2025; no urine albumin, eye exam or vaccinations recorded.

items.says: Your stool test (FIT) on 4 November 2025 was positive, and no colonoscopy or other follow-up is recorded since.
items.why: A positive FIT needs colonoscopy to check the bowel for cancer or polyps. The result is recorded as positive, and no follow-up procedure appears in the records, which cover to 2026.

facts.says: The FIT stool test result is positive.

absences.what: A colonoscopy or other follow-up bowel test after the positive stool test
absences.coverage: Her whole pod: procedures, reports, lab results, conditions, medications and immunizations, from 2022 to now

knowledge.says: A positive FIT is followed by colonoscopy, usually within a few weeks, to look for colorectal cancer and polyps. Delay matters because the test can be positive from a cancer or a precancerous polyp.
knowledge.guideline: US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer: colonoscopy after a positive FIT

items.says: Your diabetes blood sugar test (HbA1c) is overdue. The last one was 6.9% on 16 February 2026.
items.why: HbA1c is usually checked every three to six months in type 2 diabetes. Nothing has been recorded for about eight months, and your readings have moved between 6.5% and 8.3% over the years.

facts.says: HbA1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026, the most recent result.

absences.coverage: Her whole pod: lab results, from 2023 to now

knowledge.says: For type 2 diabetes, HbA1c is checked at least twice a year when the level is steady at goal, and every three months when treatment is changing or the level is above goal.
knowledge.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes

items.says: Your LDL cholesterol has not been rechecked since you started atorvastatin in February 2025.
items.why: Your LDL was 131 mg/dL (high) the day before atorvastatin was prescribed. No cholesterol test is recorded since, so the statin's effect is unknown.

facts.says: LDL cholesterol was 131 mg/dL on 18 February 2025, flagged high.
Atorvastatin 20 mg was prescribed, written on 20 February 2025.

absences.what: A cholesterol panel or LDL test after starting atorvastatin
absences.coverage: Her whole pod: lab results, from 2023 to now

knowledge.says: A cholesterol recheck is usually done four to twelve weeks after starting a statin, then yearly. Given your diabetes, your doctor may consider whether 20 mg is enough or whether a higher intensity is needed.
knowledge.guideline: ACC/AHA cholesterol management guideline; ADA Standards of Care

links.says: The LDL was measured the day before atorvastatin was prescribed, so it shows the level before treatment.

items.says: Your records show no diabetes medicine between April 2024 and February 2025, and your HbA1c rose to 8.3% in January 2025 during that time.
items.why: Metformin ended on 15 April 2024 and Jardiance was prescribed on 20 February 2025. The gap in between may be real or a missing record. It matters for understanding why your sugar rose.

facts.says: Metformin was completed and ended on 15 April 2024.
HbA1c was 8.3% on 13 January 2025, the highest value in the records.
Jardiance 10 mg was prescribed, written on 20 February 2025.

knowledge.says: A stop in diabetes medicine can let blood sugar rise, which fits the HbA1c values seen here. The records alone do not say whether the stop was planned.
knowledge.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes

links.says: Metformin stopped in April 2024, before the 8.3% HbA1c in January 2025.

items.says: Your records do not show a urine albumin test or an eye exam for diabetes in the past year.
items.why: Yearly kidney and eye checks are standard for type 2 diabetes. Neither appears in the records. Your kidney function numbers (creatinine and eGFR) are normal, but they do not replace the albumin test.

absences.what: A urine albumin-to-creatinine test in the past year
absences.coverage: Her whole pod: lab results, from 2023 to now

absences.what: A diabetic eye exam in the past year
absences.coverage: Her whole pod: procedures and reports, from 2022 to now

knowledge.says: People with type 2 diabetes need a yearly urine albumin-to-creatinine test and a yearly dilated eye exam, plus a foot check. These may have been done by another clinic and not shared with this pod.
knowledge.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes

items.says: Your records contain no vaccinations at all.
items.why: At 69, you are due for several vaccines, such as flu each year, shingles, pneumococcal and COVID-19. The records have an empty immunization section, which may mean they were not shared rather than not given.

absences.what: Any recorded vaccination, such as influenza, shingles, pneumococcal or COVID-19
absences.coverage: Her whole pod: the immunizations section, which holds no entries

knowledge.says: Adults aged 65 and over are usually recommended a yearly flu vaccine, a shingles vaccine, a pneumococcal vaccine, and current COVID-19 vaccination. Your doctor or pharmacist can confirm which apply.
